fact_text: The analyst builds a simple portfolio from PSX KSE-100 index weights: the largest constituents are taken, their weights are rescaled to sum to 100%, and the rescaled weights set the portfolio mix.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The rescaling multiplier equals 100 divided by the combined index weight of the selected top names, so a narrower basket gets a larger multiplier on each name's weight.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A Shariah-compliant version of the same approach uses the top names of the KMI-30 index instead of the KSE-100, with the same rescaling step applied to their weights.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the analyst's index-weight method there is no active trading: new contributions are split by the current rescaled weights, and the weights are rechecked after six months to a year and adjusted if they have shifted.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues equity beats property because in real estate the developer captures most of the gain while plot buyers earn much less, whereas a long-term shareholder earns roughly the same return as the business owner.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes that a buyer with PKR 5 million (50 lakh) can afford only about two plots, while a diversified stock portfolio can be started with about PKR 500,000.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's main test separating a strong business from an average one is pricing power, meaning the ability to raise prices without losing customers, since an index holds both kinds of company.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Buffett's pricing-power examples are a branded confectioner whose buyers pay more than for generic shops' equal-cost goods, and a city's top newspaper or TV channel that can charge advertisers more than rivals.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Buffett began buying Apple around 2013, reasoning that customers buy each new iPhone for its brand regardless of new features, which the analyst cites as evidence of Apple's pricing power.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues most businesses are inflation-protected because they can raise product prices when costs rise, so their profits grow during inflation while idle savings lose purchasing power.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says manufacturers whose plants were bought in dollars can see their profits rise some time after a currency devaluation, which he presents as one reason equities hedge against weakening money.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In a 2020 pandemic-era talk, Buffett argued that a country's top businesses keep creating wealth through world wars, Russia tensions, Japan's wartime ruin and the assassination of a US president.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cites a 100-year Credit Suisse study that he says found stocks gave the highest returns of any asset class worldwide.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's approach is to understand a company's business as an owner would and judge whether it is a strong business before investing, rather than acting on short-term price moves.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says the success ratio of short-term trading is low, so he prefers long-term holding of strong businesses over trading them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Make Stocks Portfolio in 5 minutes' (YouTube transcript, undated)
